checks: Compared every decoded JSON field and the exact UTF-8 bytes of both frozen versions. The sole change is the advances text. Candidate identity, statement, proof, dependencies, source hash and locators, and all other fields are identical. The statement and proof hashes agree with the original approval.

The new advances field asserts a strict finite bound for the certified directions, matching the theorem. It does not claim sharpness within that cone. This resolves the original review’s d=2 concern, where A₂>9/10 gives the certified nonnegative and replacement normals a leading coefficient at least (17/27)^3>Γ₂/2. The new wording correctly conditions signed-normal transfer on the replacement normal lying in the cone.

The hypotheses of the directional minimum agree, with d≥2, the complete symmetric census, central maximum R>0, nonnegative normalized u and the ratio hypothesis. Then c=Rt/a is strictly between zero and R. The radius sequence on consecutive indices has length 2N+1 and peak j=N after reindexing; apply the accepted truncation fact with exponent p=d≥2. The strict superlevel block is centered at j for every level below R, so its κⱼ is the reciprocal of its length and κⱼ(0)≥1/(2N+1). It is well-defined with zero endpoints and any peak plateau.

Multiply the truncation inequality by VCᵤ and use VQ_d(0)=M and 1−c/R=1−t/a. The remainder V Cᵤ c(R−c)^d/[R(2N+1)] is strictly positive at every allowed c. If c coincides with a sampled radius, positive-part terms at equality vanish and point values of the step coefficient do not affect integration. The endpoints c=0,R are valid in the truncation fact but excluded here. When N=0 the two terms add to V Cᵤ(R−c)^d, the exact one-fiber result.

The first three binomial terms give (1+1/d)^d≥2+(d−1)/(2d)>2. This implies Γ_d<1/2 and q>1−t>1/2. Subtracting 1−t from A_d gives (1−q)(1−2t)/(2q−1)>0, while A_d<1 is equivalent to q>1−t. Also (1−t)^(d+1)=Γ_d d/(d+1)>Γ_d/2, so B_d has positive denominator exceeding t and B_d<1. Thus 1/2<a_d<1 and normalized directions sufficiently near each coordinate vertex satisfy a≥a_d.

At a≥a_d, b≤1−a<a. The function (a−t)/(2a−1) has derivative (2t−1)/(2a−1)²<0 and equals q at a=A_d. From a≥B_d we have (1−t/a)^(d+1)≥Γ_d/2. These implications hold at equality in either threshold, where the positive finite correction still gives strictness.

Tightening the boundary to pass through y preserves orientation and decreases the cap by containment. For either pure base orientation the through-y cap contains exactly the whole own fiber and one full fiber of each reflected pair, so the mass is (M+VR^d)/2. The central boundary fiber is counted in full. This exceeds (Γ_d/2)M; translating a containing cap only increases mass.

For a negative coefficient vᵢ chosen minimal, the swap preserves each positive fiber and changes v to the nonzero nonnegative vector w with wᵢ=−vᵢ and wⱼ=vⱼ−vᵢ. The swapped margin equals βk+w·(x−y_cont)+vᵢ(r_k−R). The final term is nonnegative by vᵢ<0 and r_k≤R. The comparison cap drops this term, and normalizing by ∑wⱼ keeps a single shared tilt across the census. Zero-radius fibers have zero mass. The bound transfers when max(w)/∑wⱼ≥a_d, including equality. If the minimum coefficient ties, the normalized coefficient multiset is unchanged by the choice of minimizing index.

Piecewise-linear interpolation on [−N,N] has nonincreasing slopes and is nonnegative; its simplex subgraph is convex and compact. A neighborhood at base zero of a point with xᵢ>0 and ∑xᵢ<R gives interior when N≥1. Integer sampling gives exactly the 2N+1 stated fibers including zero-radius singleton endpoints and no exterior bases. For N=0 the product with [−1/2,1/2] gives exactly base zero. The indicated affine maps preserve the base and multiply each fiber volume by the same absolute determinant.

Verified source 8c5bbb9eb6411d6e §2 (6) and §3 (7)–(8) and its archived hash. The exact cap term and cone constants match. The draft adds the signed transfer by the accepted touching-majorant theorem and calculates the exact pure-base mass in place of the source’s weaker M/2 estimate.

The dimension cutoff matters. At d=1, N=1, R=1, radii (1/2,1,1/2) form a concave sequence and their interpolated interval body has exactly the bases −1,0,1. The through-center cap x≥1/2 has length 1/2 on the middle interval and only a null endpoint on each outer interval; M=2. Every cap through y=(0,1/2) takes at least 1/2 on the middle interval, so the marked normalized depth equals Γ₁/2=1/4. At the same c=1/2 the uncorrected scalar terms are both 1/2, and a correction of 1/12 would be false. This witness addresses the marked point and is outside both reviewed statements.

issues.defect: Calling Γ_d/2 sharp for the certified directions overstates the result. In d=2, q=1/√2<17/24 implies A₂>9/10. Every certified positive or swapped normal then has leading coefficient at least (17/27)^3>2/9=Γ₂/2, while pure base-normal caps have fraction at least 1/2. Thus the certified class has a uniform gap in d=2.
issues.proof_locator: advances metadata only, outside the statement and proof
issues.repair: Describe Γ_d/2 as the chain coefficient attained as a strict lower bound in the certified directions, without saying the coefficient is sharp in that cone.

overlap.comparison: Gives the same target coefficient for arbitrary directions and global sharpness when there are two equal central fibers. That result uses reflection at 1/2 and the base list −h,h+1; it does not establish the stated finite correction for integer reflection at 0.

Supplies exactly the finite scalar correction after the cap identity. The geometric claim adds the all-shared-tilt directional minimum and translates the two explicit normalized angular thresholds into a sufficient cone.
Controls large-coordinate caps on the half-integer-centered paired census and has a different equality classification. It does not give the finite correction at the integer-centered peak.
Gives the ordinary depth Γ_d of one simplex centroid. This covers the one-fiber baseline as a bound, but not the mixed chain or its direction-dependent coefficient.
Its exact middle-point formula in continuous dimension one agrees with the out-of-scope marked equality witness after subtracting 1/4 from heights. It has no implication for the d≥2 cone estimate.

initial_review.readability: Read “signed continuous normal” as a vector with at least one negative coefficient, the case where the cited swap applies. Its transfer hypothesis is checked on the resulting normalized vector. The out-of-scope d=1 witness does not assert sharpness for any d≥2 cone or for global maximum depth.
